title: Accounting work is blocked because the client still has not sent the right statement
job: Get complete, correctly labeled client evidence before review deadlines.
trigger: Engagement reaches work-ready date but required client documents are missing or wrong.
surfaceComplaint: We spend half the job chasing documents instead of doing accounting.
mechanism: Request lists, reminders, files and exception status are split across portals, email and workpapers. Clients cannot see what complete means and staff repeatedly interpret partial submissions.

workflow.friction: generic list hard to map to client reality

economics.painCostNote: Low-skill coordination consumes scarce staff/reviewer capacity exactly when deadlines peak.

buyer.roiLogic: Saving one staff hour across hundreds of engagements creates clear labor ROI.

distribution.acquisition: Pilot on one recurring close or tax cohort.

competitors.gap: remind without knowing if upload satisfies request

experiment.artifactRequest: request lists + uploads + chase threads + timestamps
experiment.success: ≥40% fewer staff chase touches and ≥20% faster time-to-ready
experiment.kill: existing portal already provides semantic completeness or client behavior does not improve

claims.text: Thomson Reuters reports 81% of tax/audit firm professionals regularly use AI, while firms face pressure to change workflows.
Client-document readiness is a low-regulatory wedge because it stops before accounting judgment.
